teile.einleitung: The Jaquet-Droz automata are three mechanical figures from the 18th century. They can write, draw and play music, and are on display in the Museum of Art and History in Neuchâtel.
wichtigste: The automata were built in the 18th century.
The builder was the watchmaker Pierre Jaquet-Droz with his assistants.
There are three figures: the writer, the draughtsman and the musician.
They move by means of cogwheels and springs, with no electricity at all.
The automata still work today.
You can see them in the museum in Neuchâtel.

abschnitte.text: **Pierre Jaquet-Droz** was a watchmaker from La Chaux-de-Fonds in the canton of Neuchâtel. Together with his son and other assistants, in the 18th century he built three artful **automata**. An automaton is a machine that carries out movements by itself. At that time the figures were shown and admired at royal courts all over Europe.

The **writer** dips a quill in ink and writes a text on paper. You can set which letters he writes. The **draughtsman** draws several small pictures. The **musician** plays a small organ, and as she does so her chest rises and falls as if she were breathing. Her eyes also move.

Inside the figures, thousands of small parts are at work: **cogwheels**, springs, levers and cams. A wound spring provides the power. The cams control how the arms, head and eyes move. Some people therefore call the writer an early forerunner of the computer, because it can be programmed.

gewusst: The automata are over 250 years old and are still working.
In the museum in Neuchâtel they are demonstrated regularly.

teile.einleitung: The canton of Neuchâtel lies in the west of Switzerland, in the Jura and on Lake Neuchâtel. French is spoken there, and the canton borders France.
wichtigste: The main town is the city of Neuchâtel.
French is spoken in the canton of Neuchâtel, which is part of French-speaking Switzerland (Romandie).
In the west it borders France, and part of the border is the river Doubs.
Since 1815, Neuchâtel has been a canton of the Swiss Confederation.
Until 1848 it was at the same time a principality of the King of Prussia.
On 1 March the canton celebrates the founding of the republic in 1848.
The coat of arms has three vertical stripes in green, white and red.

abschnitte.text: The canton of Neuchâtel lies on the northern shore of **Lake Neuchâtel**. This lake is the largest lake that lies entirely within Switzerland. Behind the shore, the heights of the **Jura** rise. Valleys such as the Val-de-Ruz and the Val-de-Travers lie there. In the west, the river **Doubs** forms part of the border with **France**.

Neuchâtel has a special history. From 1707 it belonged to the **King of Prussia**. In 1815 it was admitted as a canton into the **Swiss Confederation**. Even so, it remained a Prussian principality at the same time. On **1 March 1848**, the people of Neuchâtel proclaimed the **republic**. Since then this day has been a public holiday in the canton.

The coat of arms has three **vertical stripes** in green, white and red. At the top of the red stripe there is a small white cross. These colours date from the time of the republic. **French** is spoken in the canton. This makes it part of **Romandie**, French-speaking Switzerland.

The largest city is **La Chaux-de-Fonds**, high up in the Jura. Together with **Le Locle**, it is famous for the **watch industry**. The two cities were built so that watchmakers had plenty of light in their workshops. They are now UNESCO World Heritage Sites. The main town, **Neuchâtel**, lies on the lake and has a beautiful old town with a castle.

gewusst: In the Val-de-Travers lies the Creux du Van, a huge rock amphitheatre with steep walls.
For a long time Neuchâtel was both a canton and a principality, which existed nowhere else in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Vadian is the scholarly name of Joachim von Watt from St Gallen. He was a doctor, scholar and mayor, and in the 16th century he introduced the Reformation in the city of St Gallen.
wichtigste: Vadian's real name was Joachim von Watt.
He lived from 1484 to 1551 and came from St Gallen.
The name comes from his Latin name Vadianus.
He was a doctor, scholar, poet and mayor.
He introduced the Reformation in the city of St Gallen.
A monument in St Gallen recalls him.

abschnitte.text: Joachim von Watt was born in **St Gallen** in 1484. He studied at the university in **Vienna** and became a well-known scholar there. Like many scholars of his time, he gave himself a **Latin name**: Vadianus, Vadian for short. In Vienna he was even honoured as a poet and for a time was head of the university.

Later Vadian returned to St Gallen and worked as the **town doctor**. Soon he also became important in politics. He became **mayor** of the city and held this office several times. He also wrote books on history and geography. He was very curious and even climbed Mount Pilatus to study it.

Vadian was a friend of the Zurich reformer **Huldrych Zwingli**. With his help, the **Reformation** was introduced in the city of St Gallen in the 1520s. This made the city Reformed. The monastery of St Gallen, however, remained Catholic. That is why there was tension between the city and the monastery for a long time.

Vadian died in St Gallen in 1551. He gave his valuable collection of books to the city. This became the **Vadiana**, today's cantonal library. On the market square there is a **monument** to Vadian. Streets and schools also carry his name.

gewusst: Vadian's library is one of the oldest public libraries in Switzerland.
Vadian was one of the first people to climb Mount Pilatus in order to study it.

teile.einleitung: The Schiller Bell is an old bell from Schaffhausen. It was cast in 1486 and hung for a long time in the tower of the Allerheiligen Minster. Its Latin inscription is said to have inspired Friedrich Schiller to write his famous “Song of the Bell”.
wichtigste: The Schiller Bell was cast in 1486.
It hung in the Allerheiligen Minster in Schaffhausen.
It bears the inscription “Vivos voco, mortuos plango, fulgura frango”.
Schiller placed these words at the head of his “Song of the Bell”.
Today you can see the bell near the minster.

abschnitte.text: The bell was cast in **1486** for the Allerheiligen Minster in Schaffhausen. It bears a Latin inscription: “**Vivos voco, mortuos plango, fulgura frango**”. In English this means: “I call the living, I mourn the dead, I break the lightning.” This describes the tasks of a church bell: calling people to services, ringing at funerals and ringing during thunderstorms.

The poet **Friedrich Schiller** published the long poem “Das Lied von der Glocke” (“Song of the Bell”) in 1799. It describes how a bell is cast and links this to the lives of people. Schiller placed exactly the words of the Schaffhausen inscription above the poem. That is why people say this bell is supposed to have inspired him. Whether he ever saw it himself is not proven.

After centuries in the tower, the old bell was replaced by a new one at the end of the 19th century. The Schiller Bell was not melted down, however. Today it stands in the area of the **cloister** at the Allerheiligen Minster. Visitors can look at it close up there.

gewusst: In the past people believed that the ringing of bells could drive away lightning and bad weather, hence the phrase “fulgura frango”.
The Allerheiligen Minster was originally the church of a Benedictine monastery from the 11th century.

teile.einleitung: The Inn is a large river that rises in the canton of Graubünden. It flows through the whole Engadine, then through Austria and Germany until it runs into the Danube.
wichtigste: The Inn rises near the Maloja Pass in the Upper Engadine.
It flows through the whole Engadine.
The Engadine gets its name from the Inn, which is called “En” in Romansh.
After that the Inn flows through Austria, for example through Innsbruck.
At Passau in Germany it flows into the Danube.
With the Danube, its water reaches the Black Sea.

abschnitte.text: The Inn rises high in the mountains near the **Maloja Pass**. Soon after its source, it flows through the lakes of the Upper Engadine, such as Lake Sils and Lake Silvaplana. Then it goes down the valley past St Moritz. On the way it takes in many mountain streams and grows bigger and bigger.

The **Engadine** is a long high valley in the south-east of Switzerland. Its name comes from the Inn, which is called “En” in Romansh. A distinction is made between the Upper Engadine and the Lower Engadine. In the Engadine, besides German, people often speak **Romansh**, the fourth national language of Switzerland. At Martina, the Inn leaves Switzerland.

After Switzerland, the Inn flows through the **Tyrol** in Austria. The city of **Innsbruck** carries its name: it grew up at a bridge over the Inn. Later the river forms part of the border between Austria and Germany. In the city of **Passau** in Bavaria, it flows into the Danube.

abschnitte.titel: As far as the Black Sea
abschnitte.text: Most Swiss rivers flow via the Rhine into the North Sea or via the Rhône into the Mediterranean. The Inn is different. Via the **Danube**, its water travels through several countries to the **Black Sea**. A raindrop from the Engadine therefore has a very long way ahead of it.

gewusst: In Passau, the Inn often carries more water than the Danube, into which it flows.
The water of the Inn is very pale and greenish, because it carries a lot of fine rock dust from the Alps.

teile.einleitung: Schabziger is a special cheese from the canton of Glarus. It is green, shaped like a small cone and has a very strong, spicy flavour. It gets its colour from a herb called Schabziger clover.
wichtigste: Schabziger comes from the canton of Glarus.
It is green because Schabziger clover is mixed into it.
It has the shape of a small cone, called a “Stöckli”.
It is made from skimmed milk.
It is usually grated and eaten, for example, with butter on bread.
It is considered one of the oldest brand products in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: Schabziger is no ordinary cheese. It is hard, **green** and shaped like a small cone. This shape is called a **Stöckli**. Its taste is strong and spicy. That is why people usually eat only a little of it at a time.

To make Schabziger you need **skimmed milk**, that is, milk without cream. From it you get **Ziger**, a kind of fresh cheese. The Ziger matures for some time. Then it is ground, mixed with salt and dried **Schabziger clover** and pressed into the cone shape.

Schabziger has a very long tradition. As early as the year **1463**, the Glarus **Landsgemeinde** (open-air assembly) passed rules for how it was made and marked. That is why it counts as one of the oldest brand products in Switzerland. In the past it was traded far beyond Glarus.

Schabziger is mostly **grated**. Mixed with butter it makes **Zigerbutter**, which is spread on bread. You can also sprinkle it over pasta, potatoes or soup. In Glarus there is even a special grater for it.

gewusst: Schabziger contains almost no fat, because it is made from skimmed milk.
In English the cheese is sometimes called “Sapsago”.

t1djmf0o.t: International Committee of the Red Cross

teile.einleitung: The International Committee of the Red Cross, ICRC for short, is an aid organisation based in Geneva. It was founded in 1863 and helps people who suffer because of wars and armed conflicts.
wichtigste: The ICRC was founded in Geneva in 1863.
Henry Dunant gave the impetus for it.
Its emblem is a red cross on a white background, the reversed Swiss flag.
The ICRC helps the injured, prisoners and people in war zones.
It works to make sure the Geneva Conventions are respected.
The ICRC is neutral and does not take sides.

abschnitte.text: In 1859, after a battle at Solferino in Italy, the Geneva businessman **Henry Dunant** saw thousands of wounded men whom hardly anyone was looking after. He helped others to care for them. He wrote a book about it: “A Memory of Solferino”. In it he suggested founding relief societies in all countries. In 1901, Dunant received the first **Nobel Peace Prize**.

In 1863, Dunant and four other people from Geneva founded a committee, often called the **Committee of Five**. General Guillaume-Henri Dufour was also part of it. This committee became the International Committee of the Red Cross. As early as 1864, several states signed the first **Geneva Convention**. It requires that wounded soldiers are protected and cared for.

As the protective emblem, a **red cross on a white background** was chosen. This is the Swiss flag with the colours swapped, as an honour to Switzerland. Anyone wearing this emblem is not to be attacked in war. Later the **Red Crescent**, which many countries use, was added.

The ICRC visits **prisoners of war** and makes sure they are treated humanely. It helps families who were separated in war to get back in touch. It brings water, food and medical help to war zones. **Neutrality** is important: the ICRC helps all people in need, no matter which side they are on.

gewusst: The ICRC has received the Nobel Peace Prize three times.
In Geneva there is a museum about the Red Cross and the Red Crescent.

teile.einleitung: Schaffhausen is the main town of the canton of Schaffhausen and has the same name as the canton. The town lies right on the Rhine in the north of Switzerland. It is known for its old town, the round Munot fortress and the nearby Rhine Falls.
wichtigste: Schaffhausen is the main town of the canton of the same name.
The town lies on the Rhine.
The canton lies almost entirely north of the Rhine and mostly borders Germany.
The town's landmark is the Munot, a round fortress.
In the old town there are many houses with ornate oriel windows.
The Rhine Falls at Neuhausen are very close by.

abschnitte.titel: A town thanks to the Rhine
abschnitte.text: Schaffhausen grew up at an important spot on the **Rhine**. Downstream lie the **Rhine Falls**, which no ships can pass. So goods had to be unloaded here and carried on by cart. Trade made the town rich in the Middle Ages. The name probably recalls the boat houses where goods were stored.

High above the old town stands the **Munot**, a round fortress. It was built in the 16th century. From the tower there is a wide view over the town and the Rhine. Every evening the **Munotglöggli** (little Munot bell) rings there. In the past it signalled that the town gates and inns were being closed.

The old town of Schaffhausen is well preserved. Many houses have colourful façades and richly decorated **oriel windows**, that is, small projecting bays with windows. That is why Schaffhausen is also called the **oriel town**. A well-known building is the House of the Knight with its painted façade. The Allerheiligen Minster used to be a monastery.

Schaffhausen joined the **Swiss Confederation** in 1501. The canton lies almost entirely north of the Rhine and is mostly surrounded by **Germany**. The town is a centre of industry, trade and culture. By train you can quickly reach Zurich, but also Germany.

gewusst: The Rhine Falls at Neuhausen are considered the largest waterfall in central Europe in terms of the amount of water.
In the Second World War, Schaffhausen was bombed by mistake by American aircraft in 1944.

teile.einleitung: IWC Schaffhausen is a well-known watch brand based in the city of Schaffhausen. The company was founded in 1868 by an American and still makes expensive mechanical watches today.
wichtigste: IWC is based in the city of Schaffhausen.
The company was founded in 1868.
The founder was the American watchmaker Florentine Ariosto Jones.
IWC stands for “International Watch Company”.
The company makes expensive mechanical watches.
It is one of the few large watch brands in German-speaking Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: The watchmaker **Florentine Ariosto Jones** came to Switzerland from the USA. He wanted to combine good Swiss craftsmanship with modern machines. In 1868 he founded the **International Watch Company**, IWC for short, in Schaffhausen. The watches were mainly to be sold in America. That is why the company still has an English name today.

Most Swiss watch companies are in French-speaking Switzerland and in the Jura. Schaffhausen, however, offered something special: the **Rhine**. The power of the water could be used to drive machines. There were also workers in the area. This is how a large watch factory came to be built on the bank of the Rhine.

IWC mainly makes **mechanical watches**, which run without a battery. Inside, tiny cogwheels and springs do the work. The brand is known for pilot's watches and sturdy watches with many functions. The watches are very expensive, because a lot of handwork goes into them. Today IWC belongs to a large group, but it still produces in Schaffhausen.

gewusst: A mechanical watch can consist of hundreds of individual parts.
IWC is one of the few large watch brands that do not come from French-speaking Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Porrentruy Castle towers above the old town of Porrentruy in the canton of Jura. In German the town is called Pruntrut. From the 16th century the castle was the main residence of the Prince-Bishops of Basel.
wichtigste: Porrentruy (German: Pruntrut) lies in the canton of Jura.
The castle stands on a hill above the old town.
After the Reformation in Basel the Prince-Bishops moved to Porrentruy.
From here they ruled their prince-bishopric until the French Revolution.
The oldest part is a round tower from the Middle Ages.
Today the castle is used by the canton of Jura.

abschnitte.text: The **Prince-Bishops of Basel** were not only church leaders but also worldly rulers. They owned a territory, the **Prince-Bishopric of Basel**, which included the present-day Jura. When Basel became Protestant around 1529, the Catholic bishops could no longer stay in the city. They moved to **Porrentruy**.

The castle was extended to become the **residence** of the Prince-Bishops. From here they ruled their land for over 250 years. The oldest part is the round **Tour Réfous** from the Middle Ages. Alongside it, residential buildings, courtyards and gardens were added. From the castle you can look out over the roofs of the old town.

During the **French Revolution**, French troops occupied the territory. The last Prince-Bishop had to flee, and the prince-bishopric came to an end. After 1815 the Jura went to the canton of **Bern**. Only in 1979 did the Jura become a canton of its own.

Today the **canton of Jura** uses the castle, among other things for parts of the administration and the archive. The old town of Porrentruy has many beautiful buildings from the time of the Prince-Bishops. Porrentruy lies in the **Ajoie**, in the far north-west of Switzerland, close to France.

gewusst: The canton of Jura is the youngest canton in Switzerland; it was created in 1979.
The Ajoie around Porrentruy borders France on three sides.

teile.einleitung: Lake Sarnen is a lake in the canton of Obwalden. At its northern end lies Sarnen, the main town of the canton. In summer it is popular for swimming, rowing and sailing.
wichtigste: Lake Sarnen is in the canton of Obwalden.
Sarnen, the main town, lies at the northern end.
Other municipalities on the lake are Sachseln and Giswil.
The lake is several kilometres long.
The Sarner Aa flows into the lake and out of it again.
In summer people swim, row and sail here.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Sarnen** lies in a valley between green hills and mountains. **Sarnen** is in the north, **Sachseln** on the eastern shore and **Giswil** in the south. The **Sarner Aa** flows into the lake from the south and leaves it again at Sarnen. The lake was formed after the last ice age, when the glacier retreated.

In summer Lake Sarnen is a popular place for day trips. There are **lido pools** and places for barbecues. A lot of **rowing** is done on the lake, because the calm water is ideal for it. Sailing boats and stand-up paddlers are out too. A passenger boat crosses the lake in summer.

**Sachseln** lies on the shore. This is where the grave of **Niklaus von Flüe** can be found, who is called Brother Klaus. He lived in the 15th century and is the patron saint of Switzerland. Many people therefore visit Sachseln and nearby Flüeli-Ranft.

The **Brünig railway** runs along the eastern shore of the lake. It links Lucerne with Interlaken by way of the Brünig Pass. From the train you have a lovely view of the lake. The main road also follows the shore.

gewusst: Brother Klaus was declared a saint in 1947.
Sachseln on Lake Sarnen is an important place of pilgrimage in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Jean Tinguely was a Swiss artist who was born in Fribourg in 1925. He became famous for machine sculptures that move, squeak and clatter.
wichtigste: Jean Tinguely was born in Fribourg in 1925 and grew up in Basel.
He built moving sculptures from metal, wheels and scrap.
His art is often called kinetic art, that is art with movement.
He was married to the artist Niki de Saint Phalle.
In Basel there is the Museum Tinguely.
He died in 1991.

abschnitte.text: Jean Tinguely was born in **Fribourg** in 1925. He grew up in **Basel**, where he did an apprenticeship as a window dresser. Later he moved to **Paris**, which was then an important city for art. There he found friends among artists who wanted to try out new things. Soon he became known all over the world.

Tinguely built **machine sculptures** from wheels, belts, motors and old pieces of metal. They turn, rattle, squeak and sometimes make completely pointless movements. With them he wanted to show that machines can also be playful and funny. This art is called **kinetic art**. In 1960 in New York, he even built a machine that destroyed itself.

Tinguely was married to the artist **Niki de Saint Phalle**. She was known for colourful, round figures. Together they created works, for example a fountain in Paris with colourful figures and moving machines. In Fribourg, the **Espace Jean Tinguely et Niki de Saint Phalle** recalls the two of them.

In Basel, Tinguely's **Carnival Fountain** stands in front of the theatre, where machines spray water in all directions. On the Rhine is the **Museum Tinguely**, which shows many of his works. In Zurich, his big machine “Heureka” stands on the lakeshore. Tinguely died in Bern in 1991.

gewusst: Many machines in the Museum Tinguely can be switched on yourself with a button.
Tinguely often used scrap and found objects for his works of art.

teile.einleitung: The Jurassic is a period of Earth's history in which many dinosaurs lived. This period is named after the Jura mountains, because typical rocks from this time were found there.
wichtigste: The Jurassic is a period of Earth's history.
It began about 200 million years ago and lasted about 55 million years.
It lies between the Triassic and the Cretaceous.
It is named after the Jura mountains in Switzerland and France.
Many dinosaurs lived in this period.
Large parts of Europe were covered by shallow seas at that time.

abschnitte.text: Experts divide the long history of the Earth into **periods**. The **Jurassic** began about 200 million years ago and ended about 145 million years ago. Before it came the **Triassic**, and after it came the **Cretaceous**. Together, these three periods make up the Mesozoic Era. It is the age of the dinosaurs.

In the **Jura mountains** there are thick layers of limestone. Researchers found out that these layers come from a particular period of Earth's history. So they named this period after the mountains. Similar rocks from the same time can also be found in many other places in the world. This is how the name **Jurassic** became known worldwide.

In the Jurassic, many **dinosaurs** lived. Huge plant-eaters with long necks, the **sauropods**, ate leaves from tall trees. Brachiosaurus is one of them. Stegosaurus, with plates on its back, also lived then. Meat-eaters such as Allosaurus hunted on two legs. There were also already small mammals.

At that time the climate was warm, and shallow **seas** covered large parts of Europe. **Ammonites**, animals with coiled shells that are often found fossilised today, lived in them. Large marine reptiles such as ichthyosaurs also swam there. The **Archaeopteryx**, an early bird with feathers and teeth, also comes from the Jurassic. It was found in Germany.

gewusst: The film title “Jurassic Park” comes from the English word for the Jurassic.
Ammonites from the Jurassic can also be found in Switzerland, for example in the Jura.

teile.einleitung: The Saut du Doubs is a waterfall on the border between the canton of Neuchâtel and France. Here the Doubs plunges about 27 metres. You can reach it, for example, by boat from Les Brenets.
wichtigste: The Saut du Doubs is a waterfall on the River Doubs.
It lies on the border between Switzerland and France.
On the Swiss side lies the canton of Neuchâtel.
The water falls about 27 metres.
Above the fall lies the Lac des Brenets.
Boats sail from Les Brenets to the waterfall.

abschnitte.text: “Saut” is French and means **leap**. At the Saut du Doubs the river leaps over a rocky edge and drops about **27 metres**. After a lot of rain or during the snowmelt, an especially large amount of water thunders down. In dry summers the waterfall sometimes almost disappears.

Above the fall the Doubs is dammed to form the **Lac des Brenets**, which in French is also called Lac de Chaillexon. Boats leave from the village of **Les Brenets** in the canton of Neuchâtel and cross the narrow lake. It lies between high rock walls. From the landing stage you can reach the waterfall on a short walk.

Here the **Doubs** forms the border between Switzerland and France. So you can visit the waterfall from both sides. There are viewpoints on the Swiss and on the French side. On the French side lies the municipality of Villers-le-Lac.

In very cold winters the Lac des Brenets can freeze over. Then you can even walk on the ice as far as the waterfall, if the authorities allow it. Sometimes large **icicles** hang from the waterfall. That is a rare and impressive sight.

gewusst: The Lac des Brenets was formed because, a long time ago, a rockfall dammed the Doubs.
The Doubs flows mostly through France, where it joins the Saône.

teile.einleitung: The Jungfraujoch is a mountain saddle between the peaks of the Jungfrau and the Mönch. At 3,454 metres above sea level, the highest railway station in Europe lies here, on the border between the cantons of Bern and Valais.
wichtigste: The Jungfraujoch station lies at 3,454 metres above sea level.
It is the highest railway station in Europe.
The Jungfrau Railway runs up from Kleine Scheidegg.
Most of the route goes through a tunnel inside the Eiger and the Mönch.
The railway opened in 1912.
From the Jungfraujoch you can see the Great Aletsch Glacier.

abschnitte.text: The **Jungfrau Railway** begins at **Kleine Scheidegg**. After a short ride, the train disappears into a long **tunnel** that runs through the **Eiger** and the **Mönch**. On the way there are stops where you can look out through windows in the rock. Building the line took many years and was very difficult. In 1912 the railway finally reached the Jungfraujoch.

abschnitte.titel: Between the Jungfrau and the Mönch
abschnitte.text: A **joch** (saddle) is a lower point between two mountain peaks. The Jungfraujoch lies between the **Jungfrau** and the **Mönch**. The border between the cantons of Bern and Valais runs here. The air is thin, so you get tired easily when walking fast. There is snow and ice almost all year round.

From the Jungfraujoch you look out over the **Great Aletsch Glacier**, the largest glacier in the Alps. It is part of the **UNESCO World Heritage Site** Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch. In the **Ice Palace** you can walk through passages dug into the glacier ice. Figures made of ice stand inside.

On a rock above the station stands the **Sphinx**, a viewing platform with a research station. There, experts measure the air and the weather, for example. Because the station is so high up, the air is very clean. In clear weather you can see from here as far as the Black Forest and France.

gewusst: The Jungfraujoch is also called the “Top of Europe”.
The train takes about half an hour to travel through the tunnel.

teile.einleitung: The Jura is a mountain range in the north-west of Switzerland. With its gentle hills, limestone cliffs and valleys, it shapes many cantons, including a large part of the canton of Basel-Landschaft.
wichtigste: The Jura stretches from the area around Geneva to northern Switzerland.
It also reaches into France and Germany.
The rock consists mainly of limestone, which was laid down in a sea.
A distinction is made between the Folded Jura with its folds and the flatter Tabular Jura.
In Basel-Landschaft there are table mountains, limestone cliffs and many cherry trees.
The Jura is lower than the Alps.

abschnitte.text: The Jura stretches in a long **arc** from the area around Geneva to Schaffhausen. It lies in Switzerland and in **France**, and in the north it reaches into **Germany**. Many cantons have a share in it, for example Vaud, Neuchâtel, Jura, Bern, Solothurn, Basel-Landschaft and Aargau. The Jura is much lower than the Alps. Its highest peaks reach only a little over 1,700 metres.

A very long time ago, a warm **sea** lay here. On its floor, the shells of sea animals and lime mud were deposited. Over time, this became **limestone**. As the Alps piled up, this rock was pushed and partly folded. That is why you often find **fossils** of sea animals in the Jura.

In the **Folded Jura**, the rock was pushed together into long folds. This created parallel mountain chains with valleys between them. In the **Tabular Jura**, the rock layers lie almost flat. Typical here are **table mountains** with flat tops and steep edges. A large part of Basel-Landschaft belongs to the Tabular Jura.

In Basel-Landschaft, many **cherry trees** grow in the valleys. In spring they blossom white, and in summer the cherries are harvested. In other parts of the Jura there are wide pastures, forests and cold winters. The **watch industry** has a long tradition in the Jura. Many people like walking on the Jura heights.

gewusst: One period of Earth's history, the Jurassic, is named after the Jura mountains.
There are many caves in the limestone of the Jura, because water can dissolve lime.

teile.einleitung: Huldrych Zwingli was the most important reformer in German-speaking Switzerland. He was born in 1484 in Wildhaus in the Toggenburg and was later a priest in Glarus and Einsiedeln. From 1519 he preached at the Grossmünster in Zurich and changed the Church there.
wichtigste: Huldrych Zwingli was born in 1484 in Wildhaus in the Toggenburg.
From 1506 to 1516 he was a priest in Glarus.
After that he worked in Einsiedeln.
From 1519 he preached at the Grossmünster in Zurich.
He brought the Reformation to Zurich.
He died in 1531 in the Second War of Kappel.

abschnitte.text: **Huldrych Zwingli** was born in **1484** in **Wildhaus** in the Toggenburg, in what is now the canton of St Gallen. His father was a farmer and a respected man in the village. Zwingli was a good pupil and was able to study in Basel, Bern and Vienna. You can still visit his birthplace in Wildhaus today.

From **1506** to **1516**, Zwingli was **priest in Glarus** for ten years. During this time he read a great deal, especially the writings of the scholar **Erasmus of Rotterdam** and the Bible in its original languages. He also accompanied mercenaries from Glarus to Italy and afterwards became an opponent of the mercenary system. In 1516 he moved to **Einsiedeln**, a well-known place of pilgrimage.

From **1519**, Zwingli preached at the **Grossmünster** in **Zurich**. He explained the Bible chapter by chapter and criticised customs of the Church of the time that he could not find in the Bible. In time, the Zurich council decided to renew the Church according to his ideas. For example, pictures were removed from the churches and services were held in German. This change is called the **Reformation**.

Not all the states of the Confederation followed the Reformation. In particular, the states of central Switzerland stayed with the old faith, that is, **Catholic**. The conflict led to wars. In **1531**, Zwingli lost his life in the **Second War of Kappel**, near Kappel am Albis. His work in Zurich was carried on by his successor **Heinrich Bullinger**.

gewusst: Under Zwingli, a German Bible translation of its own was produced, which is now called the Zurich Bible.
A public sausage meal during Lent in 1522 in Zurich is regarded as one of the beginnings of the Zurich Reformation.

teile.einleitung: The Battle of Grandson took place in 1476 in what is now the canton of Vaud. The Confederates defeated the army of Charles the Bold, Duke of Burgundy. It is part of the Burgundian Wars.
wichtigste: The Battle of Grandson took place on 2 March 1476.
Grandson lies on Lake Neuchâtel in what is now the canton of Vaud.
The Confederates' opponent was Charles the Bold, Duke of Burgundy.
The Confederates won the battle.
They captured valuable treasures, the Burgundian booty.
The battle is part of the Burgundian Wars.

abschnitte.text: **Charles the Bold** was Duke of **Burgundy** and one of the richest rulers in Europe. He wanted to enlarge his realm and in doing so fell out with the Confederates. This is how the **Burgundian Wars** began. Bern and its allies feared that Charles would become too powerful.

At the start of 1476 Charles marched to **Lake Neuchâtel** with a large army and captured the castle of **Grandson**. On **2 March 1476** the Confederates met the Burgundian army nearby. A battle followed, and the Burgundians fled. The Confederates had won.

As he fled, Charles left his whole camp behind. The Confederates found magnificent tents, cannons, tapestries, jewellery and money. These treasures are called the **Burgundian booty**. Some pieces can still be seen today in museums, for example in the Bern Historical Museum.

Only a few months later Charles also lost the **Battle of Murten**. At the start of 1477 he died in the Battle of **Nancy**. After that Burgundy was no longer a danger to the Confederates. The victories made the Confederate fighters famous throughout Europe.

gewusst: Grandson Castle still stands on the shore of Lake Neuchâtel today and can be visited.
The Burgundian Wars are often summed up in a saying: Charles lost his goods at Grandson, his courage at Murten and his blood at Nancy.

teile.einleitung: The Battle of Morgarten took place in 1315 near Lake Ägeri, on the border of what are now the cantons of Schwyz and Zug. The Confederates defeated an army of the Habsburgs there. Afterwards Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden renewed their alliance.
wichtigste: The Battle of Morgarten took place on 15 November 1315.
It was fought near Lake Ägeri, on the border of what are now the cantons of Schwyz and Zug.
The opponents were the Confederates and a Habsburg army under Duke Leopold.
The Confederates won the battle.
Soon afterwards Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden renewed their alliance in the Pact of Brunnen.
A monument and a chapel recall the battle today.

abschnitte.text: For a long time there had been a dispute between the people of **Schwyz** and the monastery of Einsiedeln over pastures and forests. The **Habsburgs** were the protectors of the monastery and wanted to secure their power in the area. So **Duke Leopold** marched against Schwyz with an army of knights. The route led along Lake Ägeri towards Morgarten.

On **15 November 1315** the Confederates waited on the steep slope of Morgarten. Between the mountain and the lake the path was very narrow. The heavily armoured knights could hardly move there. The Confederates attacked from above and won the battle. Many soldiers of the Habsburg army lost their lives.

A few weeks after the battle, Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden met in **Brunnen**. There they renewed their alliance in the **Pact of Brunnen**. They promised to go on helping one another and not to make their own agreements with foreign lords. The victory strengthened the unity of the Confederates.

On the Zug side, a large **Morgarten Monument** has stood since the early 20th century. On the Schwyz side, the **Battle Chapel** recalls the event. Every year in November the **Morgarten shoot** takes place. Historians still debate where exactly the battle took place.

gewusst: The Battle of Morgarten is considered the first great battle of the Confederates.
The exact site of the battle is not known for certain, so places in both cantons commemorate it.

teile.einleitung: The Jet d'eau is a huge fountain of water in Lake Geneva. It is the landmark of the city of Geneva and shoots water about 140 metres into the air.
wichtigste: The Jet d'eau stands in Lake Geneva, in the harbour basin of Geneva.
It shoots the water about 140 metres high.
The name is French and means “jet of water”.
The very first Jet d'eau in 1886 was a pressure relief valve.
Because people liked it, it became a sight to see.
Today powerful pumps drive the lake water up into the air.

abschnitte.text: The Jet d'eau stands on the shore in the **harbour basin** of Geneva, where the Rhône leaves Lake Geneva. It shoots the water about **140 metres** high. That is higher than most church towers. You can see the jet from far away, for example from an aeroplane. In the evening it is often lit up in colour.

The very first Jet d'eau came about in **1886** at a waterworks on the Rhône. When the factories switched off their machines in the evening, the pressure in the water pipes rose too high. So a **pressure relief valve** was built, from which the surplus water sprayed into the air. People liked this jet so much that they wanted to keep it.

A few years later, the Jet d'eau was moved to its present place in the **lake**, where it could spray much higher. Today powerful **pumps** drive the lake water upwards with great force. In this way it became the **landmark** of Geneva. It appears in many photos, postcards and posters of the city.

In strong wind, the Jet d'eau is sometimes switched off or turned down. Otherwise the wind would blow the water far over the people walking along the shore. In frost it is also switched off. Anyone who goes close still often gets a little wet. On sunny days you often see a **rainbow** in the spray.

gewusst: The water leaves the nozzle at about 200 kilometres per hour.
A drop of water takes several seconds to get back down into the lake.

teile.einleitung: The Sarner Aa is a river in the canton of Obwalden. It flows out of Lake Sarnen, through the main town of Sarnen, and into Lake Alpnach. Lake Alpnach is part of Lake Lucerne.
wichtigste: The Sarner Aa is a river in the canton of Obwalden.
It leaves Lake Sarnen at Sarnen.
It flows into Lake Alpnach at Alpnach.
Lake Alpnach is part of Lake Lucerne.
After heavy rain the Sarner Aa can flood.

abschnitte.text: The **Sarner Aa** links two lakes. It flows out of the northern end of **Lake Sarnen** and through Sarnen. Then it crosses the flat valley as far as **Alpnach**, where it flows into **Lake Alpnach**. Its water thus reaches Lake Lucerne and finally, by way of the Reuss, the Rhine.

The word **Aa** is a very old word for water or river. In central Switzerland several rivers have this name, for example the Engelberger Aa. So that they can be told apart, the name of the place or valley comes first. That is how the name Sarner Aa came about.

After heavy rain Lake Sarnen rises and the Sarner Aa can burst its banks. In 2005 there was a serious **flood** in which parts of Sarnen were under water. Since then a great deal has been done for **flood protection**. Among other things, a tunnel was planned and built to carry excess water past the town.

gewusst: The water of the Sarner Aa flows through Lake Lucerne, the Reuss, the Aare and the Rhine all the way to the North Sea.

teile.einleitung: Jean-Jacques Rousseau was a famous philosopher and writer. He was born in Geneva in 1712 and wrote important books on education and on how people live together.
wichtigste: Rousseau was born in Geneva in 1712 and died in France in 1778.
He was a philosopher, writer and also a composer.
His book “Emile” is about the education of children.
In the book “The Social Contract” he wrote about the state and freedom.
His ideas influenced the French Revolution.
In Geneva there is an island with his statue.

abschnitte.text: Jean-Jacques Rousseau was born in **Geneva** in 1712. His father was a watchmaker. As a teenager, Rousseau left the city and travelled around a lot. He lived for a long time in France, especially in **Paris**. There he got to know important thinkers of his time and began to write.

In 1762 his book **“Emile, or On Education”** appeared. In it Rousseau explained that children think differently from adults. They should not simply be made to learn things by heart. Children should learn from their own experiences, as far as possible in nature. These ideas were new at the time and later influenced many educators, including the Swiss Johann Heinrich Pestalozzi.

In the same year, **“The Social Contract”** appeared. In it Rousseau asked how people can live freely and yet together in one state. His answer: power should come from the **people**, and the laws should serve the common good. These ideas were dangerous for the rulers of the time. His books were banned in Geneva and Paris.

Rousseau's ideas influenced the **French Revolution** and thinking about **democracy**. For a time he also lived on St Peter's Island in Lake Biel. He died in France in 1778. In Geneva, the **Île Rousseau**, a small island in the Rhône, recalls him with a statue.

gewusst: Rousseau also composed music and even wrote an opera.
Although Geneva once banned his books, the city is proud of him today.

teile.einleitung: Hallwyl Castle is a famous moated castle in the canton of Aargau. It stands close to Lake Hallwil on two small islands and is completely surrounded by water. Today it is a museum.
wichtigste: Hallwyl Castle stands near Seengen in the canton of Aargau.
It lies at the northern end of Lake Hallwil.
The castle stands on two islands in the Aabach.
It is one of the best-known moated castles in Switzerland.
For centuries it belonged to the Hallwyl family.
Today it is a museum and part of Museum Aargau.

abschnitte.text: A **moated castle** is a fortress surrounded by water. Hallwyl Castle stands on **two small islands** in the Aabach, which flows out of Lake Hallwil. In the past the water protected the castle from attackers. You reach the castle by bridges.

The castle was built in the Middle Ages. For many centuries the **Hallwyl family**, a well-known noble family, lived here. The castle was rebuilt and extended several times. At the start of the 20th century the family had the castle thoroughly **restored**. Later it handed the castle over to a foundation, and today it is looked after by the canton of Aargau.

Today Hallwyl Castle is a **museum**. In its rooms you can find out how the family lived over the centuries. You can see furniture, clothes, tools and toys. An old mill also belongs to the site. There are guided tours and activities for children.

The castle lies in green countryside by **Lake Hallwil**. You can walk along the lake or take a boat trip. In summer there is sometimes theatre or music in the castle courtyard. So a visit combines history and nature.

gewusst: Lake Hallwil takes its name from the same family as the castle.
Hallwyl Castle is often counted among the most beautiful moated castles in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: “Schellen-Ursli” is one of the best-known Swiss picture books. It tells of a boy from the Engadine who fetches a big bell. The book came out in 1945 and is still read with pleasure today.
wichtigste: The story was written by Selina Chönz.
The pictures were painted by Alois Carigiet.
The book came out in 1945.
It is set in the Engadine in the canton of Graubünden, in the village of Guarda.
Ursli fetches a big bell for the custom of Chalandamarz.
In 2015 the story was made into a cinema film.

abschnitte.text: Little **Ursli** is only to get a tiny bell for the Chalandamarz procession. The other children laugh at him. So he climbs alone through the deep snow up to the **mountain hut** where a big bell hangs. He spends the night there while his parents worry. The next morning he comes back with the biggest bell and gets to lead the procession.

The story was written by **Selina Chönz**, an author from the Engadine. The pictures were painted by **Alois Carigiet**, an artist from Graubünden. His colourful, warm pictures made the book famous. The two later created further books, for example about Ursli's sister Flurina.

**Chalandamarz** means “first of March”. On this day in the Engadine and in other parts of Graubünden, children walk through the village with bells and cowbells. They sing songs and want to **drive away winter** with the noise. The custom is very old and is still celebrated today.

The story is set in **Guarda** in the Lower Engadine. The village has beautiful old **Engadine houses** with thick walls and decorated façades. Many visitors come here to see Schellen-Ursli's village. A trail with stations recalls the story.

gewusst: The book has been translated into many languages, including English, where the boy is called “Ursli” and the story “A Bell for Ursli”.
The name Chalandamarz comes from the Latin word for the first day of a month.

teile.einleitung: Jurassica is a museum in Porrentruy in the canton of Jura. It shows finds from the time of the dinosaurs, above all thousands of footprints that were discovered when the A16 motorway was built.
wichtigste: Jurassica is in Porrentruy, in German Pruntrut, in the canton of Jura.
When the A16 motorway was built, thousands of dinosaur footprints were found.
The footprints are many millions of years old and date from the Jurassic.
At that time the coast of a warm sea lay here.
The museum shows fossils, footprints and a botanical garden.

abschnitte.text: When the **A16 motorway** was being built in the canton of Jura, experts examined the ground before building began. In doing so, they made a great discovery: **thousands of dinosaur footprints** in the limestone. The footprints are many millions of years old. Some come from huge plant-eaters with long necks, others from meat-eaters that walked on two legs. Many footprints form long trails, as if the animals had only just walked past.

In the **Jurassic**, the area looked completely different. The coast of a warm, shallow **sea** lay here. The dinosaurs walked across soft, muddy ground on the shore. The mud later turned into hard limestone, and the imprints were preserved. Besides footprints, fossilised bones, teeth, turtles and sea animals were also found.

In the **Jurassica** museum you can look at the finds and learn a lot about the Jurassic. It shows fossils, models and casts of the footprints. The museum also has a **botanical garden**. So here you get to know plants of today and animals from prehistoric times.

gewusst: The canton of Jura and the Jurassic both bear the name of the Jura mountains.
From footprints, experts can tell how big a dinosaur was and how fast it walked.

teile.einleitung: Interlaken is a town in the Bernese Oberland in the canton of Bern. It lies between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz and is one of the best-known holiday resorts in Switzerland.
wichtigste: Interlaken lies between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz.
The name means “between the lakes”.
The flat land between the lakes is called the Bödeli.
Interlaken is a gateway to the Jungfrau region.
Many visitors from all over the world come here on holiday.
In the middle of the town lies the big meadow called the Höhematte.

abschnitte.text: Interlaken lies on a flat plain between **Lake Thun** and **Lake Brienz**. This plain is called the **Bödeli**. It was formed because streams deposited gravel and sand over a long time. The Aare links the two lakes and flows right through the town. High mountains rise all around.

The name comes from **Latin**: “inter lacus” means “between the lakes”. In the past there was a monastery here that carried this name. The place itself was long called something else. Only later did it get the name Interlaken, which is known around the world today.

abschnitte.titel: A holiday resort for a long time
abschnitte.text: As early as the 19th century, many travellers came to Interlaken. Large **hotels** with views of the mountains were built. From Interlaken, railways run into the **Jungfrau region**, for example to Grindelwald, Lauterbrunnen and up to the Jungfraujoch. Today visitors come from all over the world. Many also do adventure sports here, such as paragliding.

In the middle of the town lies the **Höhematte**, a large meadow. It may not be built on. From here you can see the snowy **Jungfrau** in fine weather. Paragliders often land on the meadow. Old hotels stand around it.

gewusst: Above Interlaken lies the viewpoint Harder, which you reach by funicular railway.
Interlaken has two big railway stations: Interlaken West and Interlaken Ost.

teile.einleitung: Jeremias Gotthelf is the pen name of Albert Bitzius. He was a pastor in the Emmental in the canton of Bern and wrote famous novels about the life of farmers.
wichtigste: Jeremias Gotthelf's real name was Albert Bitzius.
He lived from 1797 to 1854.
He was a pastor in Lützelflüh in the Emmental.
His books tell of the life of farmers and farmhands in the Emmental.
Well-known works are “Uli the Farmhand” and “The Black Spider”.
He is regarded as one of the most important Swiss writers.

abschnitte.text: Albert Bitzius was born in **Murten** in 1797. Like his father, he became a **pastor**. From 1832 he worked in **Lützelflüh** in the Emmental. There he got to know the life of farming families well. He also campaigned strongly for schools and for poor children.

abschnitte.titel: A name from his first book
abschnitte.text: In 1837 his first novel, **“Der Bauernspiegel”** (“The Farmer's Mirror”), appeared. The narrator in it is called **Jeremias Gotthelf**. Bitzius then used this name for all his books. Soon people knew him mainly by this name. He wrote a great deal, often alongside his work as a pastor.

In **“Uli der Knecht”** (“Uli the Farmhand”), a young farmhand becomes a capable man through hard work and honesty. The eerie tale **“Die schwarze Spinne”** (“The Black Spider”) is about an old legend and about courage and trust in God. Gotthelf described farms, festivals, work and the worries of people very precisely. Sometimes he had his characters speak **Bernese German**.

Gotthelf died in Lützelflüh in 1854. His books are still read today and have been filmed several times. In Lützelflüh there is a **Gotthelf Centre** with an exhibition about his life. Many people still link the Emmental with his stories today.

gewusst: “The Black Spider” is regarded as one of the best-known tales in German-language literature.
Many Swiss know Gotthelf's stories mainly from the films.

teile.einleitung: Nidwalden is a small canton in central Switzerland on Lake Lucerne. Together with Obwalden, it used to form the land of Unterwalden, one of the founding states of the Swiss Confederation.
wichtigste: The main town of Nidwalden is Stans.
German is spoken, in everyday life the Nidwalden dialect.
The coat of arms shows a white double key on a red background.
The key is the symbol of Saint Peter.
Nidwalden belongs to Unterwalden, one of the three original cantons.
Well-known mountains are the Stanserhorn and the Bürgenstock.

abschnitte.text: Nidwalden lies on the southern shore of **Lake Lucerne** in central Switzerland. The name means “nid dem Wald”, that is, below the forest. The main town is **Stans**. Other places include Hergiswil, Buochs and Beckenried. Neighbouring cantons include Obwalden, Lucerne, Uri and Bern.

The coat of arms of Nidwalden shows a white **double key** on a red background. The key is the symbol of **Saint Peter**. According to old belief, Peter keeps the keys to heaven. Obwalden also has a key in its coat of arms, but in different colours. This shows that the two cantons belong closely together.

Nidwalden and Obwalden together formed the land of **Unterwalden**. Together with Uri and Schwyz, Unterwalden is one of the three **original cantons** that are known from the Federal Charter of 1291. Later, Nidwalden and Obwalden separated into two half-cantons of their own. Today they are simply called cantons. In Stans there is a monument to **Arnold Winkelried**, a hero from an old legend.

A cable car with an open upper deck, where you stand in the open air, runs up the **Stanserhorn**. The **Bürgenstock** is a mountain right on the lake with hotels and a rock path. **Mount Pilatus** also borders Nidwalden. A well-known aircraft manufacturer also has its base in Stans.

gewusst: The cable car up the Stanserhorn was the first cable car in the world with an open upper deck.
Nidwalden is one of the smaller cantons of Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Schabziger clover is a spicy herb. Dried and ground, it gives Glarus Schabziger its green colour and strong aroma. The plant is related to clover.
wichtigste: Schabziger clover is an annual plant.
It belongs to the legume family, like clover and peas.
It has small blue flowers.
When dried it smells very strong and spicy.
It makes Schabziger green and gives it its flavour.
It is also called blue fenugreek.

abschnitte.text: **Schabziger clover** grows to about knee height. Its leaves consist of three small leaflets, like those of clover. In summer it bears small **blue flowers**. The plant lives for only one year, so it has to be sown again every year. Afterwards it forms small pods containing seeds.

For Schabziger the plants are harvested, **dried** and finely ground. The green powder is mixed with the Ziger. This gives the cheese its **green colour**. The spicy smell, which is a little like hay, also comes from the clover.

The herb is not only used in Glarus. In the **Tyrol** and **South Tyrol** it is called **bread clover**. There it is mixed into bread dough so that the bread tastes more savoury. Some people also put it in herb butter or soups.

gewusst: Schabziger clover is closely related to fenugreek, whose seeds are used in curries.
Dried Schabziger clover keeps its aroma for a very long time.

teile.einleitung: Gruyères Castle stands on a hill above the little town of Gruyères in the canton of Fribourg. The famous Gruyère cheese is also named after the town. Today the castle is a museum.
wichtigste: Gruyères is called Greyerz in German.
The little town lies on a hill in the Gruyère region in the canton of Fribourg.
Gruyères Castle towers above the town.
In the Middle Ages the Counts of Gruyères lived here.
Today the castle belongs to the canton of Fribourg and is a museum.
The cheese Le Gruyère is named after the region.

abschnitte.text: **Gruyères Castle** was built in the Middle Ages. For a long time the **Counts of Gruyères**, who ruled the area, lived here. Later it passed to Fribourg. Since the 20th century it has belonged to the **canton of Fribourg**. In the castle you can see splendid halls, old furniture and works of art.

The little town of **Gruyères** consists mainly of a broad main street with old houses and a fountain. Cars are not allowed in. From above you can see across the green **Gruyère region** to the Fribourg Alps. Every year a great many tourists from all over the world come here.

**Gruyère** is a hard cheese named after this area. It is made from cow's milk and matures for many months. At the foot of the hill there is a **show dairy** where you can watch cheese being made. Meringues with thick **Gruyère double cream** are also well known.

Besides the castle, Gruyères has other museums. One shows works by the artist **HR Giger**, who designed fantastic, slightly eerie figures. A **crane** can be seen on the coat of arms of the counts and of the region. That fits the name, because “grue” is the French word for crane.

gewusst: The cheese Le Gruyère has a protected designation of origin (AOP), so it may only be made in a certain area.
Lake Gruyère nearby is a reservoir on the Sarine.
